subject: Deployment onramp playlist and risk acceptance
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Perez <alex.perez@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment onramp playlist and risk acceptance

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To keep momentum toward the private deployment cutover, I put together an onramp playlist (attached) and a short set of items we need to confirm for risk acceptance before we schedule day-zero tests. Can you confirm the items below or point me to the right person who owns them?

Quick checklist (high level) — please reply inline where possible:
- Network CIDR(s) and whether the subnets are already reserved for the Redwood enclave.
- Firewall egress rules (allowed destinations/ports) and whether there is a central outbound proxy.
- Private peering / VPN termination details and expected uptime SLA.
- KMS access & key rotation policy (who holds the KMS admin).
- Service account model and whether we should use cross-account roles or a dedicated service principal.
- DNS delegation for internal FQDNs and whether split-horizon is in use.
- NAT/egress IPs — we need stable IPs for allowlisting our callbacks.
- NTP and time sync policy across your environ.
- Any filtering / TLS inspection that may affect gRPC or long-lived connections.

Attachments referenced in the checklist: onramp-checklist-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with gate questions).

If helpful, Ben can run a short connectivity sweep with your network engineer this week.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm owners and provide the topology PDF if available.
2) We add any missing risks to the short acceptance doc.
3) Schedule a 60-minute day-zero runbook walkthrough (we can do Wed or Thu).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Perez <alex.perez@horizonhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment onramp playlist and risk acceptance

Karthik —

Appreciate the checklist. Quick answers inline below and attaching our network diagram for reference.

- CIDR(s): 10.20.0.0/16 reserved for the enclave; we've carved 10.20.64.0/26 for vendor access.
- Firewall: Outbound is allowed through a centralized proxy at 10.1.2.3; egress ports 443 and 53 only.
- Peering: IPsec VPN termination at our edge firewall (maintained by infra team); uptime target is 99.9%.
- KMS: We use our cloud KMS; key admin is the security team (security-keys@horizonhealth.com).
- Service accounts: We prefer dedicated service principals per vendor; ok for Redwood to create a principal and we will provision minimal roles.
- DNS: Split-horizon is used for internal names; we can add delegation entries for three FQDNs.
- NAT IPs: We have two stable egress IPs: 34.72.11.19 and 34.72.11.20.
- NTP: Internal NTP servers sync to stratum-1; available to enclaves.
- TLS inspection: There is TLS inspection on outbound when policies trigger; we can whitelist long-lived connections for Redwood if needed.

I'll loop in procurement for contractual risk acceptance and the infra lead (cc'd to procurement). Attached: org-networking-topology.pdf.

— Alex
Alex Perez
Director of Cloud Architecture
Horizon Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Perez <alex.perez@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2028-07-24T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment onramp playlist and risk acceptance

Thanks Alex — that's very helpful. A couple follow-ups and asks so we can convert this to an acceptance record:

- Can procurement confirm they accept Redwood's minimal outbound-ip requirement for webhooks (we listed the two IPs in the checklist)?
- Kimberly / Ben: can your team sign off on the TLS inspection exception for the Redwood long-lived gRPC channel? We will limit the connection to the service principal and IPs above.
- Alex: would you be able to share a contact for the infra engineer who manages IPsec terminations (we may ask for a short <30min key-exchange test window during smoke tests).

I also added two risks to the attached checklist under "Network constraints" — please review and mark "accepted" or "mitigated" in the spreadsheet. If acceptable, we'll produce a one-page risk acceptance statement that procurement can sign and attach to the deal.

Ben: when you have a slot, please propose a 30–45 min internal sweep (egress checks + TLS inspection probe).

Karthik
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Perez <alex.perez@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment onramp playlist and risk acceptance

On it — I can run the sweep tomorrow morning PST. Plan:
- Validate egress IPs from a test enclave instance.
- Verify TLS handshake behavior through their proxy (short-lived and long-lived).
- Confirm DNS resolution for the three delegated FQDNs.
- Smoke test a small tokenized call to the Redwood callback endpoint.

I'll upload results to the shared drive and link in the HubSpot deal. If I hit anything blocking (TLS interception failure or unexpected port restrictions) I'll flag and request a short triage call.

Attachments: none for this message.

— Ben
Senior Activation Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Perez <alex.perez@horizonhealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment onramp playlist and risk acceptance

Alex / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Alex, and thanks Ben for owning the sweep. Procurement (cc'd earlier) — once you confirm acceptance of the two egress IPs we will prepare the formal risk acceptance statement and aim to schedule the day-zero runbook walkthrough.

Proposed meeting: Thu 2028-07-26 10:00–11:00 PT (Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210). Please let me know if that works and we'll send a calendar invite.

HubSpot: I'll add the checklist snapshot and the sweep results to HH-7842 after Ben uploads.

Kimberly Park
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
